solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finally putting spotlight on boy vocalist

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows it
in an across clue, one thing on another is written after it, so the boy comes first

blocks.note: a boy is a son
last letter of putting
to spotlight or stress something is to emphasise it

explanation.surface: A boy singer at last gets his moment in the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' looks like part of the phrase 'putting spotlight on', but it only donates its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A songstress is a female singer, so the word is a feminine synonym for a vocalist.

clue.text: Band of commandos with horse

blocks.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service commando regiment
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A unit of commandos rides out on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of soldiers, but it is a strip of cloth; horse is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Old lady extremely cold in buff

blocks.note: a nan is a grandmother
a keen wind is a bitingly cold one

explanation.surface: Granny is freezing while sitting around naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In buff' suggests in the nude, but buff is the colour being defined; keen describes piercingly cold air.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, and the name is also used for its pale buff colour.

clue.text: Business processing pilchards and hens

indicators.note: processing food breaks it down and reworks it, so the letters that follow are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
joins the two words of fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm that processes fish and poultry for the food trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's chandler is a shop or dealer supplying stores and equipment to vessels, so it is a kind of business.

clue.text: Wild kid, full of spirit

indicators.note: something full of a substance holds it inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: to kid or rag someone is to tease them
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: An unruly child has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging and wild both describe something violent and out of control, such as a storm.

clue.text: Most cosy and intimate around noon

indicators.note: around says one word wraps round the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: to intimate something is to hint at or suggest it
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A cosy, intimate midday moment together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' reads as an adjective alongside cosy, but it is the verb meaning to hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means warm and comfortable, so its superlative is a synonym for most cosy.

clue.text: Leaders of agricultural co-ops are introducing berry from Brazil

indicators.note: leaders are the front-runners, so the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Farm cooperatives are bringing a Brazilian superfood to market.
explanation.definitionFit: The acai is a small purple palm berry from the Amazon, popular as a health food.

clue.text: Dream of clock perhaps on top of abbey

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

blocks.note: a clock that strikes the hours is something that chimes; perhaps flags it as an example
first letter of abbey

explanation.surface: A chiming clock in an abbey tower gives someone a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fantasy or illusion, the same sense as an impossible dream.

clue.text: I get in mood ridiculously early

indicators.note: something done ridiculously is absurd and disordered, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits they get in a happy mood absurdly early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in good time is to arrive with time to spare, which is to be early.

clue.text: Registered grand French monarch

blocks.note: when a fact has sunk in, it has registered
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A grand French king is formally recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Registered grand' looks like a description of the monarch; it is sunk in plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun King was the nickname of Louis XIV of France, who chose the sun as his emblem.

clue.text: African animal returned to eat kill, cause of downfall

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the animal's name is read right to left
to eat something is to take it inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: the gnu or wildebeest is an African antelope
to do in is to kill

explanation.surface: A wildebeest's return to feed on a kill leads to its ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's undoing is whatever brings about their ruin or downfall.

clue.text: Eminent detective used insight at work

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being moved about, so these are rearranged

blocks.note: a DI is a detective inspector
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated detective applied insight on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished and eminent both describe someone respected and prominent in their field.

clue.text: Unruly passenger blocked by old VIPs

indicators.note: an unruly person will not stay in order, so the letters are scrambled
a road blocked by something has it sitting in the middle, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A disruptive passenger is held back by old dignitaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Personages are important or distinguished people, the same as VIPs.

clue.text: Engagement's beginning with flash rock

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of engagement
in a flash or a mo means in a moment

explanation.surface: An engagement starts with a flashy diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' paired with engagement and flash suggests a diamond ring, but it is the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Emo is a style of emotional, confessional rock music that grew out of punk.

clue.text: Companion and I about to stop Gypsy reading palms

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece is pushed into the middle of the other

blocks.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
taken as written
Romany is the name of the Gypsy people and their language
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A friend and I visit a fortune teller to have our palms read.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiromancy is palmistry, telling fortunes from the lines of the hand.

clue.text: Honourable silence socially acceptable in part of Japan

blocks.note: Hon is the abbreviation for Honourable
sh is a call for silence
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Respectful silence is good manners in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of Japan's main islands, home to Tokyo.

clue.text: Hopeful when Private Eye published second of stories

indicators.note: second of means just the letter in position two of the next word

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a PI is a private investigator
a paper that ran a story published it
second letter of stories

explanation.surface: An ambitious writer waits for the satirical magazine Private Eye to run their stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine, which makes 'published' and 'stories' look natural, but here it is a private detective.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone who aspires to a position, a hopeful candidate.

clue.text: Repetition that is catching start of hypnotic state

indicators.note: catching only the start means the outer word grips just the opening letter, and the rest follows on

blocks.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
a trance is a hypnotic state

explanation.surface: Repeating a phrase brings on a hypnotic trance.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter of the trance goes inside I.E.; the remaining letters trail after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterance is a rare word for iteration, the act of doing or saying something again.

clue.text: Ponder something of conundrum in a text

indicators.note: something of means a part taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: sits across conundRUM IN A TExt

explanation.surface: Think over a puzzle sent by text message.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to think deeply and at length, which is to ponder.

clue.text: Extremely eager dog restrained by gracious Queen's lead

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters stay
something restrained is held in, so these letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: outer letters of eager
a cur is a mongrel dog
'Gracious!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A keen dog is held back on a lead by a kindly queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's lead' looks like the monarch walking a dog; it is the frontman of the rock band Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Mercury was the lead singer of the band Queen.

clue.text: Beaming head off, do well at golf in the morning

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: an eagle is two under par on a hole
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A golfer is beaming after a fine round played that morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means shining or gleaming, which is what something beaming does.

clue.text: Nation raising tax on 50 per cent of realty

indicators.note: raising a word in a down entry lifts it so it reads bottom to top
fifty per cent is half, so only the first half of the word is used

blocks.note: to tax someone is to tire them out
first half of realty

explanation.surface: A country imposes a property tax at half the value of real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy, which suits the property surface, but here it is the verb meaning to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea.

clue.text: Nightmares including tumbril on a regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: inc. is short for including
second, fourth and sixth letters of tumbril

explanation.surface: Bad dreams regularly involve the cart taking you to the guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: A tumbril is the cart that carried the condemned to execution in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi were demons thought to press on sleepers, and the word came to mean nightmares.

clue.text: Spoil sleeve when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter moves round to the front

blocks.note: the arm of a garment is its sleeve

explanation.surface: A sleeve gets ruined while riding a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests catching a sleeve in a bicycle chain; it means the letters rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to damage or spoil the look or quality of something.

clue.text: A tiny girl's furious complaint

indicators.note: something furious is in a wild state, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small girl is screaming an angry protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is an ailment, and furious screaming could cause it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is inflammation of the voice box, and complaint is an everyday word for an illness.

clue.text: Sums up case of Alfred Dreyfus's framing

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the two end letters are used
a frame surrounds a picture, so only the edge letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: outer letters of Alfred
outer letters of Dreyfus's

explanation.surface: A summary of the Dreyfus affair, in which Alfred Dreyfus was framed for treason.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Dreyfus was a French army officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894, so 'case' and 'framing' fit the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To add numbers is to total them, which is to sum them up.

clue.text: Time to enter cell — it's free of charge

indicators.note: to enter is to go in, so this letter is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: a neuron is a nerve cell
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It's time to go into a prison cell, and at least it costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free of charge' sounds like costing nothing; it means having no electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge, hence its name.

clue.text: Led journalist to the back of Poe's house

blocks.note: Poe wrote the story The Fall of the House of Usher
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter was shown round the rear of Edgar Allan Poe's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to lead or escort them to a place.

clue.text: Pair of oafs each hiding baby's first toy

indicators.note: each one hiding something keeps it out of view, so that letter disappears from both copies of the word
'first' keeps only the first letter of 'baby'

blocks.note: a yob is a loutish oaf
a pair means the oaf appears twice
first letter of baby

explanation.surface: Two louts each conceal a toddler's first plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is British slang for a lout; with the B taken from each, two YOs remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spinning toy that climbs and drops on a string.

clue.text: In arrears, graduate banker is at last jailed

indicators.note: at last means the closing letter of each word just before it is taken

blocks.note: behind with payments means in arrears
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
last letters of banker and is

explanation.surface: A banker who fell into debt has finally been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars is an idiom for being in prison, which is to be jailed.
